lessons.title: जवळ (javaḷ) — near, close to
lessons.gloss: near, close to — the postposition a direction-asker actually gets answered with

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Last chapter stacked things above and below each other. Real directions are almost never that tidy.

segments.instruction: say khālī, then var, then bend घर and glue each on
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *khālī*, then *var*, then bend **घर** and glue each on]

segments.text: जवळ — javaḷ — near, close to.
माझं घर पुण्याजवळ आहे. — mājhaṁ ghar puṇyājavaḷ āhe. — my house is near Pune.

This is the answer a real person gives when you ask कुठे? and the true answer is not a single named point. It takes the same oblique stem as everything else in this column — पुणे becomes पुण्या- — so nothing new has to be learned about the noun.

जवळ (javaḷ) carries the ळ, the retroflex l that is Marathi's own letter and that Hindi does not have. Say it with the tongue curled back, the way you learned it in chapter three, or the word will sound like a different one.
It has a second job you will need in the next chapter: X जवळ (javaḷ) can also mean in X's keeping — near enough to reach — which is how Marathi gets close to saying somebody HAS something.

segments.instruction: javaḷ — near, with the tongue curled on the ळ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *javaḷ* — near, with the tongue curled on the **ळ**]

segments.prompt: Say that your house is near Pune.

feedback.correct: A location given without a street.
feedback.incorrect: puṇe bends to puṇyā- before javaḷ.

segments.text: Which letter in जवळ (javaḷ) is the one Hindi does not have? (ळ.) What does पुणे become before it? (पुण्या-.)
Sources: Wiktionary: जवळ (javaḷ).

lessons.title: समोर (samor) — in front of, opposite
lessons.gloss: in front of, opposite, facing — and a word built out of a face you have already been taught

segments.text: जवळ (javaḷ) says close by, which does not say which side.
समोर — samor — in front of, opposite, facing.
घरासमोर — gharāsamor — in front of the house.
This is the postposition a set of directions is actually made of. Opposite the station, in front of the shop — a Marathi speaker giving you a landmark reaches for समोर (samor) before anything else.

Take the word apart and it pays you back. It is Sanskrit सम्मुख (sammukha) — सम् together plus मुख face. Chapter nineteen told you that मुख is the formal doublet of तोंड, the everyday mouth. So समोर (samor) is, quite literally, face-to-face: the thing whose face is turned toward yours.
That is why it means opposite as well as in front of. English keeps those apart; Marathi does not need to, because a face has only one direction.

segments.instruction: gharāsamor, then gharājavaḷ — a side, then a distance
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *gharāsamor*, then *gharājavaḷ* — a side, then a distance]

segments.instruction: which body part is inside this word — मुख, the formal tond
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which body part is inside this word — ***मुख***, the formal *tond*]

segments.prompt: Say 'in front of the house' and 'near the house', and name the difference.

feedback.correct: One names a side; the other only a distance.
feedback.incorrect: Same stem gharā-; only the tail changes.

segments.text: What two pieces is समोर (samor) built from? (सम् together and मुख face.) Why does one word cover both in front of and opposite? (A face points one way; both meanings are that.)
Sources: Wiktionary: समोर (samor).

lessons.title: लांब (lāmb) — far, and long
lessons.gloss: far, and also long — one Marathi word where English needs two, and the answer to how far

segments.text: जवळ (javaḷ) answers near. Nothing yet answers the other half of the question.
लांब — lāmb — far; long.
माझं घर लांब आहे. — mājhaṁ ghar lāmb āhe. — my house is far away.

लांब (lāmb) is जवळ (javaḷ)'s opposite and does not behave like it. जवळ (javaḷ) is a postposition and wants a noun bent in front of it; लांब (lāmb) is an ordinary word that can simply stand in the sentence, which is why the example above needs no oblique stem at all.

The second meaning is the one to hold onto, because it explains the first. Sanskrit लम्ब (lamba) means "hanging down, extended" — so लांब (lāmb) is long before it is far, and far is only long applied to a distance. A Marathi speaker uses the one word for a long rope and a distant town without feeling any jump.
Pair the two and you can answer a real question:
जवळ, की लांब? — javaḷ, kī lāmb? — near, or far?

segments.instruction: javaḷ, kī lāmb? — and answer it about where you live
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *javaḷ, kī lāmb?* — and answer it about where you live]

segments.prompt: Say that your house is far, then that it is near Pune.
acceptedResponses: mājhaṁ ghar lāmb āhe; mājhaṁ ghar puṇyājavaḷ āhe
माझं घर लांब आहे माझं घर पुण्याजवळ आहे

feedback.correct: One needs no stem; the other does.
feedback.incorrect: lāmb stands alone; javaḷ needs puṇyā- in front of it.

segments.text: Which of जवळ (javaḷ) and लांब (lāmb) needs the oblique stem? (जवळ (javaḷ) — it is a postposition; लांब (lāmb) is not.) What does लांब (lāmb) mean before it means far? (Long.)
Sources: Wiktionary: लांब (lāmb).

lessons.title: Give somebody a direction
lessons.gloss: a distance, a side, and the other end of the distance — enough to give a direction

segments.text: Three words landed in this chapter and only two of them are postpositions. Name all three, then say which one is the odd one out and why.

segments.instruction: ghar kuṭhe āhe? — then answer puṇyājavaḷ
khoolīsamor — in front of the room
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *khoolīsamor* — in front of the room]

segments.instruction: lāmb — and notice you added no ending to anything
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *lāmb* — and notice you added no ending to anything]

segments.instruction: ask kadhī? and kitī? about the same house
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: ask *kadhī?* and *kitī?* about the same house]

segments.prompt: Ask where a house is, then answer three ways: near Pune, in front of the room, far.
acceptedResponses: ghar kuṭhe āhe? — puṇyājavaḷ; khoolīsamor; lāmb
घर कुठे आहे? पुण्याजवळ खोलीसमोर लांब

feedback.correct: A distance, a side, and the far end.
feedback.incorrect: Two of the three bend the noun in front of them; lāmb does not.

segments.text: You can now answer कुठे? five ways without naming a street. Which of this chapter's three words is not a postposition? (लांब (lāmb).)
